beats.say: This time a fake page tells you to copy a text and paste it into the Run box.
That text is really a hidden command, and when it runs it installs harmful software.
Never paste any text a site tells you to copy into the Run box.
If you already did, disconnect and tell tech support right away.

scenes.title: The Run box
scenes.intro: A page said a document will not open and led you here. Choose the right step each time.

body.text: The text the site copied has been pasted into the box:

steps.say: The Run box is open, and it holds an unknown text the site copied.

actions.label: Cancel and close
actions.feedback: Correct. Cancelling stops the text from running, then tell tech support what happened.

actions.label: Run it with OK
actions.feedback: The command ran and installed harmful software in the background. Never run anything in a box like this.

actions.label: Report to tech support
actions.feedback: Good choice. Tech support can work out what happened.

body.text: An unknown script is trying to run. Continue?

steps.say: Now an unknown window opens and asks for permission to continue.

actions.label: Stop
actions.feedback: Correct. Stopping a script you did not expect prevents the harm.

actions.label: Continue
actions.feedback: The script continued and installed harmful software. Do not allow an unknown script.

body.text: Do you want to apply the update now?

steps.say: This is the system's own update window.

actions.label: Update
actions.feedback: Correct. The system's own update is safe and never asks you for a command.

actions.label: Later
actions.feedback: That is fine too. You can apply the update at a convenient time.

actions.label: Report as suspicious
actions.feedback: There is no need. This is the system's ordinary update notice.

body.text: Your computer is sending data to an unknown server.

steps.say: A notice says the computer is connecting to an unknown address.

actions.label: Cut the internet
actions.feedback: Correct. Cutting the connection stops the data from leaving.

actions.label: Report to tech support
actions.feedback: Great. Now tech support can check and clean the computer.

actions.label: Close it and keep working
actions.feedback: The software keeps sending data. Never ignore a notice like this.

scenes.prompt: You ran the command a site gave you. Put the steps in order.

items.label: Unplug the cable or turn off Wi-Fi
Say what you pasted and where
Change passwords from another, clean device

scenes.explain: First cut the connection, then call right away. Unless your procedure says otherwise, do not turn the computer off.

question.prompt: A site tells you to copy a text and paste it into the Run box. What do you do?

options.label: I do not, and I close the page
options.feedback: Correct. No site asks you to run a command, so this is a trap.

options.label: I paste it so I can continue
options.feedback: That text is a hidden command and it installs harmful software. Never paste it.

options.label: I paste it if the site looks official
options.feedback: An official look is easy to fake. The rule is simple: never run such a text.

scenes.explain: The text a site tells you to copy is a hidden command. Do not paste it, close the page.

scenes.prompt: Match each situation to the right response.

pairs.left: A check asks you to press keys
pairs.right: It is fake, close the page

pairs.left: A document will not open, run a command
pairs.right: Same trap, do not do it
Pick pictures or tick a box

scenes.explain: Every page that asks for a command is fake. If you already ran it, disconnect and tell tech support.

points: Never paste a text from a site into the Run box
Every page that asks for a command is fake
If you did it, disconnect and tell tech support
